haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image without pushing and runs unit tests only, never deploying. A merge to main starts the full pipeline that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA>, built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: A failed integration test gets one automatic retry; if it fails again, the run ends. A failed unit test gets no retry and ends the run. Nothing reaches staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the image it ran before this run, restored by deploy.sh rollback staging. That image is found from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers members who are not the commit author may approve, in the CI UI. With no approval in 72 hours, the run expires and nothing reaches production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, under /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. Only deploy.sh writes them, after a successful stable rollout or a rollback. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable deployment is untouched, SSM tags are unchanged, and the schema stays migrated, since migrations are forward-only and not reverted.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded and posts a notice to #deploys. This covers runs waiting for approval, the window, or the lock.
haiku-low.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until inside Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC with the production lock free. Approvals do not expire.
haiku-low.q10: Canary 5xx ratio is queried from Prometheus by the canary-watch step every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. One reading above 1%, or no data, fails it at once.
haiku-low.q11: The run posts to #deploys with IMAGE_TAG, a link to smoke results, and commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG. Approvers approve in the CI UI.
haiku-low.q12: Staging: kubectl rollout undo returns pods to the prior image, since SSM was not written and still names it; rollback would go one version too far. Production: kubectl rollout undo, then canary-off. No reason stated.

sonnet.q1: A pull request runs build (image not pushed) and unit tests only, posting a status; it never deploys. A merge to `main` starts the full pipeline.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the image built once per run and pushed as registry.internal/shop-api:<commit SHA> (IMAGE_TAG). Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry; if the retry fails the run fails. A unit test failure gets no retry and the run fails. Either final failure ends the run, nothing reaches staging, and the failing step is posted to the deploys channel.
sonnet.q4: It runs `deploy.sh rollback staging`, which restores the SSM previous_tag, the image staging ran before this run. The run then fails and is posted to the deploys channel.
sonnet.q5: A `release-approvers` member who is not the commit author, approving in the CI UI. If no approval within 72 hours the run ends as expired, posts to #deploys, nothing goes to production, and staging keeps the image.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store under `/deploy/<env>/current_tag` and `/deploy/<env>/previous_tag`. Only deploy.sh writes them: after a successful stable rollout (`deploy.sh <env> <tag>`), and on `deploy.sh rollback <env>` (current_tag set back to previous_tag). The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment untouched, SSM tags unchanged, and the schema stays migrated (migrations are not reverted). `deploy.sh canary-off` is run, the lock released, and the failure posted.
sonnet.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded, with a notice posted, if it has not started its production deploy (including waiting for approval, window or lock).
sonnet.q9: It waits and re-checks every 5 minutes until it is inside the start window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) and the production lock is free. The approval does not expire; e.g. Thursday-evening approval starts Monday 09:00.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio is measured. The canary-watch step queries Prometheus every 60 seconds for 15 minutes. A single reading above 1%, or a query with no data, is a failure and triggers canary-off immediately.
sonnet.q11: The run posts to the #deploys channel with IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commits between production current_tag and IMAGE_TAG. Approvers approve in the CI UI.
sonnet.q12: With `kubectl rollout undo`, which returns the environment to the pods that were running (in production followed by canary-off). SSM was not written so it still names them. `rollback` is not used because previous_tag would go one version too far back. (The document spells this reasoning out for staging only; production's rollout-failure path is stated as undo then canary-off.)
